rows.en: I saw something
I can't see anything

So you didn't actually see anything.
But you can tell this tree isn't just an ordinary cherry tree, right?
You can tell from the blossoms alone, but there's a lot more around it, things the eye can't see.
There might be loads of faces full of hatred showing up on that trunk, too...{p}

Heh heh, looks like you did see something, {c}{f:|}.
If you didn't see anything, I guess that means your sixth sense is weak.
...You've had enough now, right?
Let's go back to the club room.
We still have to hear everyone else's stories.
Who are you picking next?{p}

So you really are scared.
You know, around this tree, nothing comes near it. Not just animals, even birds and bugs stay away.
Even the stray dogs you see in empty lots never go near it, and you don't see crows flying around here either, right?
Animal instinct, I guess.
They can sense the danger.
Humans are the only ones who still want to go, even when they know better.{p}

Did you know?
Lots of people go missing around this tree.
Sometimes they get found, apparently, but every one of them is so weak it's like all the nourishment got sucked out of their bodies, and hardly any of them make it.
Even the ones who finally pulled through get tormented by visions, and they're in the hospital, or so I hear...
One of them said they could see a human face on their arm, and tried to cut it off with a box cutter.
As if you could cut off an arm with something like that.
The people around them stopped them right away, so the wound wasn't too bad, apparently.
But then, the wound talked, they say.
Twisting up hideously, it let out a shriek, 'Come quickly,' and laughed.
...Are you even more scared now?
Okay, okay, let's hurry back.
Who are you going to ask next?{p}

What's wrong?
You've had enough already?{p}
You're not going?{p}

Hmm, how boring...
Well, they do say it's better not to go near it carelessly, just out of curiosity.
Like, say you touched that cherry tree, right?
They say the skin where you touched it breaks out in a rash.
At first it just puffs up a little, but nothing you put on it makes it heal, and in the end it festers into an oozing mess. That's what I've heard.
There was someone before who touched the tree out of curiosity, and their skin festered, and they couldn't stand it anymore and cut that spot off with a box cutter.{p}

Why couldn't they stand it?
Other people couldn't see it like that, but it talked, they say, with a human face...
And it was always looking up at them with resentment, apparently.
That blackened, festering skin they'd cut off twisted its lips and said this, they say.{p}

They say schools are places where spirits gather easily.
Because that tree is pulling in the spirit paths, I think all the wandering spirits around here are gathering there too.
They say that with Kokkuri-san too, low-level spirits and animal spirits are easier to call, right?
I can't tell what kind of spirit paths run through it, but I feel like I can kind of sense a swirl of dark feelings centered on the cherry tree.
Whenever I look at that tree, I get goosebumps.
Somewhere far off in the back of my mind, an alarm goes off.
That tree is dangerous!
They say it's still on the quiet side for now.
But one of these days... the grudges of the spirits, stored up to their limit, will burst into bloom.
With malice riding on every single petal...
When that time comes, what's going to happen to this school, I wonder?
It might be tomorrow, or it might be a year from now.
Or maybe it's already...{p}

Actually, before I came here, I went to look at that tree.
It was in bloom.
It seems kind of off-season, but they say that cherry tree is like this every year.
My big sister graduated from here too.
She told me it's the cherry tree that forgets the seasons.
And so...
What kind of blossoms do you think were blooming?
Cherry blossoms, of course.{p}Don't go answering roses or tulips or something.
Ordinary cherry blossoms
Cherry blossoms filled with grudges

Good for you.
Don't worry, they were still ordinary blossoms.
Though the cherry tree itself was creepy, like always.
From now on, you'd better keep a careful eye on that tree too, {c}{f:|}.
Like, keep an observation diary or something...
Oh, that's a good one!
You totally have to do it.
And if it looks like something's about to happen, tell me, okay?
Okay, that's as far as my story goes.
Who's next?{p}

...Hmm.
So it really is like that, huh.
You know, that cherry tree's blossoms are usually a deeper color than ordinary cherry blossoms.
From far away, it looks like a red mist.
But when I saw it just now, the blossoms were white.
Like snow... is that how I'd put it?{p}

Pale, bluish-white blossoms without the slightest warmth were in full bloom.
It was beautiful, but it was a frightening sight...
The petals fluttering down felt like they were chasing me, so I hurried away from there.
Even so, petals stuck to my hair and shoulders, and they just wouldn't come off.
See, there are still some stuck on me, right?{p}

Eww, I just noticed something.
Look.
These petals... can't you see faces on them★
More like skulls than faces, maybe.
Anyway, these are blossoms full of grudges, aren't they!
Eek, I don't want them!{p}
Here, they're yours, {c}{f:|}.{p}
...Did you throw them away?
Yes
No

Thank you.
More importantly, things have gotten really bad, huh.
I mean, the grudge blossoms have bloomed.
This gathering isn't going to end safely.
I don't know what's going to happen, but I hope we get to hear everyone's stories.
Okay, that's the end of my story.
Let's hurry on to the next person.{p}
Meanie!{p}

Really?
That's great.
Telling this story was worth it, then.
Okay, try putting your hand on the tree trunk.
Try to feel the spirits even more...{p}

Close your eyes...
Open your heart...
See? Amazing, right?
They say people who see spirits here get bewitched by the cherry tree.
The spirits' grudges drag the living in, they say.
And the ones who get pulled in try to escape their suffering by calling yet another person, they say.
When they pull someone else in, they're freed from the suffering for just a little while, or so I hear...{p}

{c}{f:|}, you saw the spirits, didn't you?
Heh heh, I didn't see a thing.
But you saw them, right?
Ever since I heard this story, I've brought all kinds of people here, but you're the first one who's ever seen the spirits, {c}{f:|}.
So I don't know what happens to people who get bewitched.
Sorry.
You'll probably get dragged in.
Scary, huh.
...I see, so the rumor was true.
Well, I'm satisfied now, so shall we head back to the club room?
Heh heh, don't worry.
If anything happens to you, {c}{f:|}, I'll prove it for you.
It was the cherry tree's curse.
...Like that.
That's as far as my story goes.
Who's next...?{p}

I think so too.
No matter how you look at it, it's not normal.
I'll tell you a story about that tree.
...It's from before this school was built, so it was a really long time ago...{p}

They say there used to be a small lake around here.
That cherry tree supposedly stood on the shore of that lake, so the old school building would have been completely underwater.
Nature worship, I guess you'd call it?
It's a faith that's been around in Japan since way back, and that lake and the cherry tree were worshipped by the people back then too.
It was a local folk faith, so I think it was something simple.
Prayers for a good harvest, praying for rain, and festivals of thanks...
Ordinary stuff you'd find anywhere, right?
Loved by simple people, it must have spent its days in peace.
Yes, until that time came...{p}

One year, a famine struck the village.
The drought went on and on, the crops withered, and even the river that flowed nearby was running low.
Even so, the lake was still brimming with clear water, they say.
Thanks to that, the villagers could at least quench their thirst, apparently.
Since it was a sacred place, they held back at first, but little by little, everyone seems to have gotten more shameless.
They were greedy, weren't they.
Before long, the villagers were fighting each other over the water, and it got fiercer day by day.
As if heaven were angry at people like that, there wasn't the slightest sign of rain.
On the contrary, even the lake's water started to shrink.{p}

By then, the villagers' fighting had turned into killing each other, they say...
When a traveler passing through saw it, the villagers' corpses were scattered across the bottom of the dried-up lake, and every body was shriveled bone-dry, without a single drop of blood left in it.{p}

Right beside them, that cherry tree was apparently in magnificent full bloom.
It happened at the end of summer, too, when it wasn't blossom season at all.
It sucked up the villagers' blood and bloomed.
That's why the cherry tree here is a little deeper red.{p}
...So, scary story, right?{p}What part scared you?
Human greed
The power of nature

You think the same way I do.
Ghosts and monsters are scary too, but people really are the scariest.
Especially people possessed by greed.
They don't know any limits, right?
I'm not saying having no desires is a good thing, but hearing this story kind of makes you think, doesn't it?
You'd better remember that people can change into something else entirely.
And also that, along with the villagers' blood, that vile greed flowed into that cherry tree.
Inside that tree lives a devil, made of greed and the grudges that always come with it.
So?
Why don't we go take a look right now?{p}Take a look at what? That cherry tree, of course.
Let's go see it
I don't want to go

Right?
In the face of nature's incredible power, humans are such tiny things.
There are huge powers like drought, and there are even mysterious powers, like flowers that bloom by sucking blood from corpses.
There may not be many people who can reach a plant's heart, but most plants understand what people say, you know.
Even something humans spent long, long years building, nature can snatch away in an instant.
You've probably figured it out already, but hidden inside that cherry tree are nature's mysterious power and the bitter regret of the humans who lost to it...
You should take a good look at it sometime.
It'll overwhelm you.
Oh, I know, why don't we go see it now?{p}Come on, it can count as research for the interview too.
Let's go see it
I don't want to go

Really?
Telling this story was worth it, then.
Okay, try putting your hand on the tree trunk.
Try to feel the spirits even more...
And then, try closing your eyes.{p}

Now listen closely.
See, amazing, right?
And you know, they say once someone has seen a spirit here, they'll see all kinds of things for a while afterward.
In this world, it's often happier not to see, isn't it?
Especially at this school...
If you're stuck in a place this full of ghosts, you'll go crazy.{p}

{c}{f:|}?
You look pale.
Don't tell me you're seeing something horrible?
Oh my, that's bad.
We'd better hurry back to the club room.
Heh heh, but it's the same wherever you go, I guess...
Anyway, my story ends here.
Next person, go ahead.{p}

Really?
Telling this story was worth it, then.
Okay, try putting your hand on the tree trunk.
Try to feel the spirits even more...
And then, try closing your eyes.{p}

See, amazing, right?
And you know, they say once someone has seen a spirit here, for a while afterward, whenever they close their eyes, what they saw will float up in front of them.
Go on, try blinking...
Go on, try closing your eyes...
Can't you see it?{p}

It's a story that makes you want to cry, isn't it?
But she still clings to this world, so it seems she envies the people who are actually alive.
That's why they say it's better not to go near it carelessly, just out of curiosity.
Like, say you touched that cherry tree, right?
They say the skin where you touched it breaks out in a rash.
At first it just puffs up a little, but nothing you put on it makes it heal, and in the end it festers into an oozing mess. That's what I've heard.
There was someone before who touched the tree out of curiosity, and their skin festered, and they couldn't stand it anymore and cut that spot off with a box cutter.{p}

Why couldn't they stand it?
Other people couldn't see it like that, but it talked, they say, with a human face...
And it was always looking up at them with resentment, apparently.
That blackened, festering skin they'd cut off twisted its lips and said this, they say.
"Take me away from there..."
That's the end of my story.
Well then, next person, go ahead...{p}
